_meta.note: Make the adversarial refuter runnable on a DIFFERENT model/backend than the doer — an emergent capability that cascades from (execute/refute being separate backend methods) x (the enforced distinct-actor rule). The executor already runs the automated review under a distinct ACTOR (worker vs worker:refuter); today it dispatches `refute` on the SAME backend/cmd as `execute`, so a model can't refute its own blind spots. This adds a distinct refuter config — HB_REFUTE_BACKEND / HB_REFUTE_CMD / HB_REFUTE_MODEL / HB_REFUTE_PROVIDER (and executor.json refute_*), each FALLING BACK to the doer's value so default behavior is byte-unchanged (backward compatible). The refute dispatch routes to that config, records which model/backend refuted in the review artifact (provenance), and keeps the distinct-actor guarantee. Both runtimes (py executor.py + plugin hb-exec.js) — the refute config is a shared surface shown by `exec config` (T63 behavioral parity); the cross-model dispatch itself is runtime-local like the executor generally (parity-notes). Proof is deterministic: a doer stub + a DISTINCT refuter stub over the script wire — no model, no network — asserting the refuter stub (not the doer) produced the stored review, under a distinct actor, with provenance recorded; a control without HB_REFUTE_* shows the doer does the refute (backward compat).

tasks.title: Author the deterministic cross-model proof
tasks.description: Spec-first: write docs/howto/gate-examples/cross-model-refuter.sh (deterministic — stubs over the script wire, no model/network). Set up a review-gated project (P0, GATE_P0 with a `review` block and a passing behavioral criterion). Provide a DOER stub (HB_EXEC_CMD): execute writes the gate artifact + {ok:true}; refute → {refuted:false, findings:'DOER-STUB ... GATE_P0 ...' (>=40 chars, cites the gate)}. Provide a DISTINCT REFUTER stub (HB_REFUTE_CMD): refute → {refuted:false, findings:'REFUTER-STUB (distinct model) ... GATE_P0 ...' (>=40 chars)}. PY runtime: `HB_EXEC_CMD=doer HB_REFUTE_CMD=refuter hb exec run` → the phase COMPLETES and the stored review artifact (.hb/reviews/GATE_P0.attempt.md) contains REFUTER-STUB (the refuter ran the refute, NOT the doer), records the refuter identity (provenance), and the review_passed event's reviewer actor is DISTINCT from the doer's task_done actor. Control (PY): without HB_REFUTE_CMD, the artifact contains DOER-STUB (backward compat). Model-override coverage: the refuter stub echoes the HB_EXEC_MODEL it received into its findings; set HB_REFUTE_MODEL=<sentinel> and assert the sentinel surfaces in the stored artifact (proves the model/provider env override reaches the refute call end-to-end, since script stubs otherwise ignore the model). PLUGIN runtime: bootstrap a project, same stubs via HB_EXEC_CMD/HB_REFUTE_CMD, `node .hb/hb-exec.js run` → the artifact contains REFUTER-STUB. Print CROSS-MODEL-REFUTER-OK only if all hold.

tasks.title: Implement in the Python executor
tasks.description: In py/src/heartbeat/executor.py: config() adds refute_backend (HB_REFUTE_BACKEND / executor.json refute_backend, fallback to backend), refute_cmd (HB_REFUTE_CMD / refute_cmd, fallback to cmd), refute_model (HB_REFUTE_MODEL / refute_model, default None), refute_provider (HB_REFUTE_PROVIDER / refute_provider, default None). dispatch() gains optional model/provider params that set HB_EXEC_MODEL / HB_EXEC_PROVIDER in the env around the backend call and restore after (works for in-process and subprocess). The review_pending path builds a refute-cfg (backend=refute_backend, cmd=refute_cmd) and dispatches refute via it with model=refute_model, provider=refute_provider; write the refuter identity (backend/model) into the .hb/reviews/<gate>.attempt.md header (provenance) and log which refuter ran. Defaults unchanged when no HB_REFUTE_* set (backward compatible).

tasks.title: Mirror in the plugin executor
tasks.description: In plugin/templates/hb-exec.js: config() adds refuteBackend (HB_REFUTE_BACKEND / file.refute_backend, fallback backend), refuteCmd (HB_REFUTE_CMD / file.refute_cmd / defaultCmd(refuteBackend), fallback cmd), refuteModel (HB_REFUTE_MODEL), refuteProvider (HB_REFUTE_PROVIDER). dispatch() gains an optional extraEnv arg merged into the spawn env; the review_pending path dispatches refute via c.refuteCmd with extraEnv = {HB_EXEC_MODEL: refuteModel, HB_EXEC_PROVIDER: refuteProvider} (only keys that are set), records the refuter identity in the reviews/<gate>.attempt.md header, and keeps the distinct refuterActor. `exec config` prints the refute fields. Keep the wire/behavior identical to the Python side (parity of the shared refute-config surface).

tasks.title: Write the cross-model verification guide
tasks.description: Write docs/howto/cross-model-verification.md: the idea (the doer and the refuter can be different models, so a model's blind spots don't refute themselves — this cascades from execute/refute being separate methods + the enforced distinct-actor rule), the config (HB_REFUTE_BACKEND / HB_REFUTE_MODEL / HB_REFUTE_PROVIDER / HB_REFUTE_CMD and the executor.json refute_* keys; each falls back to the doer's so it's opt-in and backward compatible), the two guarantees it keeps (distinct actor for the review pass; the refuter identity recorded in the review artifact for provenance), and an HONEST note: the deterministic proof verifies the ROUTING + distinctness + provenance; the blind-spot-catching benefit is inherent to model diversity (not separately benchmarked). Reference gate-examples/cross-model-refuter.sh; link add-refutation-to-a-sensitive-gate.md and choose-a-backend.md. Only real commands.

assert c['refute_cmd']==c['cmd'], c
